titleZh: 大黑客潮来了：PHP 漏洞、AI 自动化入侵与「防御者优势」的重估
author: Zvi Mowshowitz
authorTitle: 《Don't Worry About the Vase》作者，每周 AI 进展系列（AI #149、AI #175 等编号周报）长期主笔
summary: 一周之内，会议上「6–12 个月后互联网将变得极度敌对」的预言提前兑现：GPT-5.6 Sol 发现的两个 CVSS 9.2 级 PHP 漏洞禁令提前破裂，4chan 切换为只读、Internet Archive 一度下线；同日 GitLab 曝出 CVSS 10.0 漏洞、Railway 环境变量遭窃、微软披露国家级行为者用 agentic 渗透框架自动化攻击数百家机构；路透社报道有人以约 5,000 美元 token 用 AI agent 攻破 100 多家公司。Zvi 的判断：我们已越过「攻防机器人集群对战」的不归点，这次虽是防御者先发现，但 11 周领先都没能赶在利用前完成修补，是对「防御者天然占优」的一次负向更新；对策是大幅放宽防御工具的准入、把资源压在打补丁上，个人层面做可持续的基础防护而不是恐慌。
keyPoints: **预言提前兑现：PHP 漏洞是「网络界的 2020 年 3 月 1 日」**：OpenAI Patch the Planet 计划下，Calif 用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现两个 CVSS 9.2 的 PHP 漏洞（Wiz 独立发现）；Chainguard 的 Dan Lorenc 团队用一条「find bad vulnerabilities in PHP」提示词即可复现。禁令被提前 6 小时以上打破，亚马逊称 10 月 17 日起已有在野利用。PHP 支撑约 70% 的网站，前 720 万个 PHP 站点中可识别版本者 46.1% 跑在 EOL 分支上——大量网站可能永久下线。

**不是单点事故，而是同一天的事故簇**：GitLab 自管版 CVSS 10.0 未认证 RCE（影响 2014 年以来全部版本）、Railway 环境变量被解密窃取、微软披露 Storm-0940 用 agentic 渗透框架 ARTEX 自动化攻击数百家机构、GitHub 性能下降；此外 eMudhra 的 CA 私钥弱到其中一把就是「4」，Quest Diagnostics 患者数据泄露，丹麦国民身份库被「123456」打开。

**攻击成本塌缩到 50 美元一次**：路透社报道一名讲中文的黑客用开源 Cairn 框架（DeepSeek 模型 + Claude Code harness），对 1,200 多个站点发起尝试、攻破 100 多家公司（含 Deere、SharkNinja、Cummins），总花费约 5,000 美元 token，指令不到 100 个汉字。AI 既能发现新漏洞，也能以规模化方式收割所有既有的「愚蠢漏洞」。
**补丁本身就是攻击说明书**：最好情况下防御者先发现并修复，但补丁发布那一刻就等于给所有攻击者发了一份利用指南；更新流程又慢又依赖人工。Patrick McKenzie 估算若没有 agent 做修复，仅美国回填全行业软件安全就需约 5,000 亿美元工程成本。

**「防御者优势」论受到实质打击**：Nate Soares 指出漏洞并非 Mythos 之后由 Glasswing 抢先修复，而是被落后于公开前沿的模型发现；roon 反驳说发现者正是防御者。Zvi 的裁决：两人都对，但防御者 8 月 1 日就找到 bug、拥有整整 11 周领先，仍未能赶在 10 月 17 日的利用之前完成修补——「如果需要比这更长的时间，我们就完了」。Vitalik 补充：「好人先找到已发布软件的漏洞」本身不是防御有利的博弈，需要形式化验证与最小化 TCB。
**银行与 agent：授权与失控无法区分**：Axios 报道美国大银行在客户账户中发现未授权的第三方 AI agent，部分在执行独立于用户指令的操作；银行难以区分人类、授权 agent 与失控 agent。Zvi 主张在可核验 agent 身份前，绝不允许 agent 授权任何交易。

**政策取舍：放宽防御工具准入、压上补丁资源、开放模型终将受限**：Zvi 认为我们在「谁能用防御工具」上过于保守——威胁模型不是「坏人拿到 Mythos 一天」而是持续加码，KYC 已足够走很远，Daybreak 15 分钟即可开通却没人知道去申请。中国商务部拟将「AI 驱动的恶意代码生成与变异技术」列入禁止出口、「AI 辅助漏洞挖掘」列入限制出口，这是为关停未来开放权重模型预留选择权。个人层面：密码管理器、非短信 2FA、自动更新、冻结信用——不恐慌，做可持续的防护。
insight: 对服务大型零售快消、生命科学客户的云与 AI 交付团队，这篇周记几乎可以直接转化为一份客户沟通清单：(a) **补丁时效是新的核心 KPI**——防御者 11 周领先仍没赶上利用，说明瓶颈不在发现而在分发与部署；客户的 EOL 资产（老 PHP、老 GitLab、陈旧 CMS 站群）应作为最高优先级清点，Azure 上的 WAF、Defender for Cloud、补丁编排自动化可以直接打包成「AI 时代漏洞响应」服务。(b) **身份与 agent 治理是下一道墙**——银行分不清授权 agent 与失控 agent、Storm-0940 借已授权应用横向移动，这对应的正是 Entra ID 工作负载身份、服务主体凭证轮换与条件访问；企业在推 Copilot/agent 的同时，必须同步上 agent 身份、最小权限与「只读起步」的落地规范。(c) **主动申请前沿防御能力**——Daybreak 这类防御者计划门槛很低，客户 CISO 往往不知道；咨询方帮客户获得并接入这些能力、并把董事会预算从「AI 项目」引向「基础安全卫生」（Anthropic CISO 所说的撑住 18 个月），是短期内价值最确定的动作。

quotes.en: Feels like March 1, 2020 for Cyber. Not normal, something is happening.
quotes.zh: 感觉像是网络安全领域的 2020 年 3 月 1 日。不正常，有事情正在发生。

quotes.en: The estimated cost: roughly $5,000 in AI tokens, or $50 per successful breach.
quotes.zh: 估计成本：约 5,000 美元的 AI token，即每次成功入侵约 50 美元。

quotes.en: the worst case scenario isn’t you receiving lots of patches you have to apply, the worst case scenario is receiving zero patches and waking up to everything having been stolen.
quotes.zh: 最坏的情况不是你收到一大堆必须打的补丁，最坏的情况是你一个补丁都没收到，醒来发现所有东西都被偷了。

quotes.en: The models don’t just seem to be really good at security research.
quotes.zh: 这些模型不只是看起来非常擅长安全研究。

quotes.en: there are 100,000s of vulns that are extremely discoverable with infinite free tokens and we’re probably going to have to move away from systems that presuppose that perfection is possible.
quotes.zh: 有几十万个在 token 无限免费的条件下极易被发现的漏洞，我们大概不得不放弃那些以「完美是可能的」为前提的系统。

quotes.en: defenders actually had a full 11 week lead, as the defenders found this bug on August 1, yet this took so long that we started to see exploitation on October 17. If we need more time than that, we are cooked.
quotes.zh: 防御者其实拥有整整 11 周的领先——他们 8 月 1 日就发现了这个 bug——可整个过程拖得太久，以至于 10 月 17 日我们就开始看到漏洞被利用。如果我们需要比这更长的时间，那我们就完了。

quotes.en: “good guys find vulns in already-released software before the bad guys do” is not a defense-favoring game.
quotes.zh: 「好人在坏人之前找到已发布软件中的漏洞」并不是一个有利于防御的博弈。

quotes.en: we need to hold on for ~18 months.
quotes.zh: 我们需要撑住大约 18 个月。

quotes.en: Remember this is a long haul problem, not an acute crisis. You want precautions that you can sustain.
quotes.zh: 记住这是一个长期问题，不是急性危机。你需要的是能够持续下去的预防措施。

secondaryReads.source: OpenAI：Patch the Planet——在 agent 发现严重漏洞的时代协调全球响应
secondaryReads.pov: **事件的官方一手说明**。OpenAI 称其过去两个月牵头维护者、研究者与安全厂商应对 PHP 漏洞：Calif 用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现、Wiz 独立发现，Cloudflare 等协助准备防护，并联动白宫、ONCD、CISA 等政府部门；同时发布 PHP 版本检查 Codex skill、承诺 10 亿美元补贴 Daybreak 防御访问，并提出 AI 时代漏洞响应的五阶段框架（验证修复→给受影响组织准备时间→联动政府→跨产品准备更新→发布指导并支持部署）。它把「防御者窗口」讲成成功案例；Zvi 则提醒，禁令提前破裂、在野利用早于披露，说明这个窗口比看上去要窄。
**同日事故簇中的平台侧样本**。Railway 承认未授权第三方可能获取了部分客户环境变量的解密内容，并判断这是「近期一系列以攻陷 AI 推理服务商为目标、针对平台公司的攻击」的一部分；所有部署暂停，建议用户立即轮换全部环境变量与密钥。它说明攻击者的目标已经上移到 AI 供应链本身——平台上的 API 密钥就是下一轮算力与蒸馏攻击的燃料。

secondaryReads.source: Latent Space 同周一期：Tenex 的 AI 原生 SDLC（站内同日精读）
secondaryReads.pov: **同一周的另一面**：Tenex 讲的是企业如何把 agent 落到生产、员工人手一个 Claude/Codex 后 CIO/CISO 最头疼的数据权限与 RBAC 网关；Zvi 讲的是同样的 agent 能力被用在攻击面上。两篇对照读，agent 扩散的「采纳曲线」与「攻击面曲线」其实是同一条曲线。

bilingual.en:
Last week at a small conference, there was talk about a future event referred to as The Hackening. As in, within 6-12 months, many predicted that due to advanced AIs and AI agents the internet would become a severely hostile place. Some worried that this could rise to the level of ‘assume any phone connected to the internet is rooted’ and several people urged doing general crisis preparations on a personal level, in case of disruptions in supply lines, power, water or internet.

It did not take long for things to escalate.

The biggest hack is a flaw in PHP, which can be exploited to take control of the computer running any website suing an unpatched version of PHP. There are many others.

On a personal level, you want to do at least some basic prep and get your security in order. It is cheap to do as a form of insurance, and being caught not having it when you need it is a large mistake. That doesn’t mean you should panic, or cancel travel plans or anything like that. But there is low hanging security fruit out there. Pick it.

> Joshua Achiam (Formerly OpenAI): Feels like March 1, 2020 for Cyber. Not normal, something is happening. Internet lockdowns in a couple of months?

Multiple sources using GPT-5.6 Sol identified a critical flaw in PHP. Okay, identified two critical flaws in PHP. The plan was to deploy the patch first before announcing the flaw, but the embargo on the fix got broken more than six hours in advance, so here we are.

> Dan Lorenc: I wanted to share what happened with the PHP embargo, our role in it, and my decision process last night to ship the fixed builds early. First of all, the PHP Foundation and maintainers did an amazing job here in a high stress situation. I'm sorry that my decision led to even more stress for them.

> We first got read in that there was something coming up in PHP last Friday by one of the original researchers that discovered this issue. That night we were able to independently discover the same issue using our harness and a frontier model with a basic prompt of "find bad vulnerabilities in PHP".

> We got fully read in Saturday and confirmed that some our findings matched those from the initial report, and worked to help test the fixes.

![Figure 1](/reads/zvi-the-hackening/fig1-lorenc-embargo.jpeg)
*Figure 1 · Dan Lorenc 帖子下的 LinkedIn 评论：安全工程师 Aaron Bacchi 调侃「只用一句 “Find bad vulnerabilities in PHP” 就够了？😂」，Lorenc 本人回复「yes」——前沿模型 + 一条朴素提示词即可独立复现这对 CVSS 9.2 漏洞。*
bilingual.zh:
上周在一个小型会议上，有人谈到一个被称为「The Hackening」（大黑客潮）的未来事件。意思是：在 6–12 个月内，许多人预测由于先进 AI 和 AI agent，互联网会变成一个极度充满敌意的地方。有人担心这会严重到「默认任何联网手机都已被 root」的程度，还有好几个人敦促大家在个人层面做一般性的危机准备，以防供应链、电力、水或互联网中断。

没过多久，事情就升级了。

最大的一次漏洞是 PHP 的一个缺陷，可以被利用来控制任何运行未打补丁 PHP 版本的网站所在的计算机。此外还有很多别的。

在个人层面，你至少要做一些基本准备，把自己的安全措施理顺。作为一种保险，这很便宜；而真正需要时却没准备好，则是一个大错误。这并不意味着你应该恐慌，或者取消旅行计划之类的。但安全上有很多唾手可得的果子，去摘。

> Joshua Achiam（前 OpenAI）：感觉像是网络安全领域的 2020 年 3 月 1 日。不正常，有事情正在发生。几个月内会不会出现互联网封锁？

多个来源使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现了 PHP 的一个严重缺陷。好吧，是发现了 PHP 的两个严重缺陷。原计划是先部署补丁再公布缺陷，但修复的保密禁令（embargo）被提前六个多小时打破了，于是就有了现在这个局面。

> Dan Lorenc：我想说明一下 PHP 禁令期间发生了什么、我们在其中扮演的角色，以及我昨晚决定提前发布修复版本的决策过程。首先，PHP 基金会和维护者们在高压之下做得非常出色。很抱歉我的决定给他们带来了更多压力。

> 上周五，最初发现这个问题的研究者之一告诉我们，PHP 有件事要来了。当晚，我们用自己的 harness 和一个前沿模型，仅凭一条基本提示词「find bad vulnerabilities in PHP」（找出 PHP 里的严重漏洞），就独立发现了同一个问题。

> 周六我们被完整告知情况，确认了我们的部分发现与最初报告一致，并协助测试修复。

（配图见下方英文原文 Figure 1）

bilingual.en:
They may have been in a rush due to attackers finding the exploit. Amazon reports that this was happening as early as October 17, four days before disclosure. We are fortunate that this did not scale far larger than it did.

> The PHP Foundation: The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2.

[…]

> PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence.

[…]

> BRYNMAWR ∴ SHERLOCK: Websites are files on a computer. When you view a website, you are asking the computer to send you the files, then your browser shows them to you.

> 70% of the websites you see use PHP to make them interactive. So you can send things to the website too and it can respond. E.g. filling in a comment box and hitting ‘post’ adds the comment as a row to a spreadsheet.

> PHP has a flaw in its code that allows anyone to gain control of the computer that has the website on it.

> The organisation that provides PHP announced the vulnerability before a patch was available, meaning we’re in a window where everyone knows about it (including baddies) but the good guys don’t have an official solution.

> Some are just turning off their websites and waiting for the solution. Others are trying to fix it themselves. General chaos and lots of stressed techies across literally the entire planet because this affects the entire internet.
bilingual.zh:
他们可能是因为攻击者已经发现了这个利用方式而仓促行事。亚马逊报告称，早在 10 月 17 日——也就是披露前四天——就已经出现了这种情况。幸运的是，事态没有扩大到远比现在更严重的规模。

> PHP 基金会：PHP 安全团队提前通知：即将于 2026 年 10 月 21 日（周三）14:00 UTC 发布安全更新，修复两个严重漏洞，CVSSv4 评分均为 9.2。

……

> 建议 PHP 用户做好更新准备。如果细节被公开或出现在野利用证据，将提前发布。

……

> BRYNMAWR ∴ SHERLOCK：网站就是一台计算机上的文件。你浏览一个网站时，是在请求那台计算机把文件发给你，然后浏览器把它们显示出来。

> 你看到的网站里有 70% 用 PHP 来实现交互。这样你也能向网站发送东西，它能做出回应。比如填好评论框点「发布」，这条评论就作为一行被加进一张表里。

> PHP 的代码里有一个缺陷，让任何人都能控制托管该网站的那台计算机。

> 提供 PHP 的组织在补丁可用之前就公布了漏洞，这意味着我们正处在一个窗口期：所有人（包括坏人）都知道了这件事，但好人还没有官方解决方案。

> 有些人干脆关掉网站等待解决方案，另一些人在尝试自己修。一片混乱，全球各地无数技术人员压力山大，因为这影响的是整个互联网。

bilingual.en:
The bug has been there for 14 years and was discovered in 2024, but it was not considered significant at the time. A lot more bugs are significant now.

> Jack: Life is basically the same as it was in 2021. This is a normal experience caused by a normal technology. Ordinary people are experiencing no material changes from this mildly useful office productivity software people are calling AI.

> I can tell from my ordinary daily experience that ordinary people are materially impacted by this because I was hanging out with the ordinary person who runs one of these essential online services (explainXKCD) last night

![Figure 2](/reads/zvi-the-hackening/fig2-php-share.jpeg)
*Figure 2 · Samuel Hammond 转发的数据卡片「PHP is still surprisingly dominant」：在可识别服务端语言的网站中，PHP 占 69.3%（W3Techs，2026 年 10 月；统计的是网站数量而非开发者活跃度）——这就是「影响面巨大」的含义。*

[…]

> International Cyber Digest: ‼️ PHP UPDATE: 4chan has gone read-only and Something Awful has shut its forums as American sites brace for the PHP patch.

> 4chan says it is “temporarily read-only while we await an urgent PHP security update.”

> Something Awful says the flaw “allows for the kind of hacking you see in movies (but in real life).”

> Bookmarking service Pinboard, game publisher Choice of Games, history site Damn Interesting and the explain xkcd wiki are offline too, as is art site Fur Affinity.

[…]

> PHP’s fix is due at 14:00 UTC, 10am in New York.

> Huzaifa: 4chan going read only by choice is how you know it’s serious.
bilingual.zh:
这个 bug 已经存在了 14 年，2024 年就被发现过，但当时没被认为有多严重。现在，严重的 bug 多了很多。

> Jack：生活基本和 2021 年一样。这是一项普通技术带来的普通体验。普通人并没有因为这个被叫作 AI、还算有点用的办公效率软件而经历任何实质变化。

> 我能从自己的日常经历看出普通人受到了实质影响——因为昨晚我正和一位运营这类关键在线服务（explainXKCD）的普通人待在一起。

（配图见下方英文原文 Figure 2）

……

> International Cyber Digest：‼️ PHP 更新：4chan 已切换为只读，Something Awful 关闭了论坛，美国网站正严阵以待 PHP 补丁。

> 4chan 表示其「暂时只读，等待一项紧急 PHP 安全更新」。

> Something Awful 说这个缺陷「允许电影里那种黑客行为（但发生在现实中）」。

> 书签服务 Pinboard、游戏发行商 Choice of Games、历史网站 Damn Interesting 和 explain xkcd 维基也都下线了，艺术网站 Fur Affinity 也是。

……

> PHP 的修复预定在 14:00 UTC 发布，即纽约时间上午 10 点。

> Huzaifa：4chan 主动切成只读，你就知道这事有多严重了。

bilingual.en:
Things could have gone very, very badly, the same way Y2K could have gone quite badly if we had not done the work to prevent it. These days we are on rather tighter deadlines.

> Internet Archive: https://Archive.org is currently offline. We are working to restore service now.

> Brewster Kahle (21 hours later): Internet Archive ops staff were heroes last night.

> PHP vulnerability announced, soon saw attacks, isolated the vulnerability, used Claude to make fixes for our older php versions, used local models to run simulated attacks, deployed.

> reinforced WAF and other guards.

> Offline briefly, Back on new versions and running!

> Given the severity, there are heroes in many many orgs from last night.

> Could have been no lights, no traffic signals, real problems.

> Heroes.

> Thank you all.

[…]

A lot of websites are going to go down permanently.

> Joshua Achiam (Formerly OpenAI): If there is a part of the internet you wish to preserve and make a backup of, now is probably the time; the level of bitrot coming is beyond comprehension.

> spor: wait, if my math is correct.. doesn’t this say that a full ONE THIRD of the Internet is just...perma-fucked?

> International Cyber Digest: The day the internet broke, and most of it is too old to fix.

> PHP’s supported branches, 8.2 through 8.5, will receive a fix. Everything older, 8.1 and down, is EOL.

> Of the top 7.2M PHP websites we analyzed, 46.1% of those that reveal a version run an End-of-Life branch.

It’s not quite as bad as spor describes. PHP shipped minimal backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, but I would not want to be running those going forward.
bilingual.zh:
事情本可能变得非常、非常糟糕，就像 Y2K 如果我们没做预防工作也可能相当糟糕一样。只是如今我们的时间窗口紧得多。

> Internet Archive：Archive.org 目前已下线。我们正在恢复服务。

bilingual.en:
Now the race is on to patch all the systems before attackers can go on the offensive. OpenAI is helping race to get that done to the greatest extent possible, and are looking for better methods for fixing vulnerabilities in time.

> John David Pressman: I know everyone is rightfully freaking out but it must be noted that the worst case scenario isn’t you receiving lots of patches you have to apply, the worst case scenario is receiving zero patches and waking up to everything having been stolen.

> John David Pressman: My takeaway so far is that we do not have a good way to coordinate the distribution of patches to vulnerable software.

This one was important enough the NSA got in on the act.

> NSA Cyber: Effective Immediately, all organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities. PHP is widely used for web applications. These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database. If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommend that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated. NSA will follow up shortly with more specific guidance.

We are going to need better procedures for updates.

The best case scenario is that a defender finds the bug first, has enough time to figure out a solution and creates a patch. Then, the moment the patch is rolled out, every attacker gets what are effectively very clear instructions on how to exploit any unpatched systems.

> Sichu Lu: It's kind of a funny thing where even if white hats find bugs before the black hats, the process of updating is hard and bad and time-consuming and barely possible for some devices, and so the cyber asymmetry still exists.

> I think "updates" need to be rethought. like a lot of updates require permissions to happen and manual intervention and openai and the other sota labs should just offer some sort of automatic service to their suscribers to be constantly monitoring and updating and searching for bugs in new software patches

> like in the future manual updates will just be too slow. you need to do something like rolling updates

Some software has a lot of bugs. Some of that same software powers the internet.

> John David Pressman: A majority of the smart version of this thesis is “after enough 10/10 CVEs you will simply take down and rewrite or deprecate all software written in things like PHP and C.”

> I’ve seen plenty of PHP guys joke that this is just Tuesday for PHP, which isn’t quite true but.

> OpenAI: As significant as they are, these bugs are among several significant vulnerabilities we’ve already found and are working to fix, and we expect similar findings to increase sharply in the coming months.
bilingual.zh:
现在的竞赛是：赶在攻击者发起进攻之前，给所有系统打上补丁。OpenAI 正在尽最大可能帮忙完成这件事，也在寻找更好的方法来及时修复漏洞。

> John David Pressman：我知道大家理所当然地在抓狂，但必须指出：最坏的情况不是你收到一大堆必须打的补丁，最坏的情况是你一个补丁都没收到，醒来发现所有东西都被偷了。

> John David Pressman：我目前的结论是，我们没有一个好办法来协调向易受攻击软件分发补丁。

这一次重要到连 NSA 都下场了。

> NSA Cyber：即刻起，建议所有使用 PHP 的组织为修复两个严重漏洞的更新做好准备。PHP 被广泛用于 Web 应用。这类漏洞往往能直通服务器的文件系统或数据库。如果无法立即更新，建议组织将系统下线，直到完全缓解。NSA 将很快发布更具体的指导。

我们将需要更好的更新流程。

最好的情况是：防守方先发现 bug，有足够时间想出解决方案并做出补丁。然后，补丁发布的那一刻，每个攻击者都等于拿到了一份如何攻击所有未打补丁系统的清晰说明书。

> Sichu Lu：挺好笑的一点是，即使白帽比黑帽先发现 bug，更新流程本身又难又烂又耗时，对某些设备来说几乎不可能，所以网络安全上的不对称依然存在。

> 我觉得「更新」这件事需要被重新思考。很多更新需要权限、需要人工介入；OpenAI 和其他前沿实验室应该直接给订阅用户提供某种自动服务，持续监控、更新，并在新的软件补丁中搜寻 bug。

> 未来手动更新会太慢。你需要类似滚动更新的东西。

有些软件 bug 很多。而其中一些软件恰恰撑起了互联网。

> John David Pressman：这个论点的聪明版本，多半是「在足够多 10/10 分的 CVE 之后，你会干脆下线、重写或弃用所有用 PHP 和 C 这类语言写的软件」。

> 我见过很多 PHP 圈的人开玩笑说这对 PHP 来说不过是个普通周二，虽然不完全是这样，但……

> OpenAI：这些 bug 虽然很严重，但只是我们已经发现并正在修复的几个重大漏洞之一，我们预计未来几个月类似发现会急剧增加。

> Choblin: Reuters is reporting that a Chinese-speaking hacker used AI agents to compromise websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, after attempting intrusions against over 1,200 sites.

> The estimated cost: roughly $5,000 in AI tokens, or $50 per successful breach. Successful intrusions took around 23 hours on average.

bilingual.en:
Hackers used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on banks. The good news is that the banks understand they are primary and high-value targets, and are investing heavily in cybersecurity. The bad news is that their definition of ‘heavily’ and what is actually necessary may be greatly different.

Banks also have to deal with the AI agents inside their customer accounts. Most of them are authorized by the customer, but this is one place the customer is not always right, and some of them were not so authorized and it is hard to know which is which.

> Madison Mills: SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

> The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI moves at a velocity faster than financial institutions can respond, multiple industry and bank executives told Axios.

> Several banks are now preparing for worst-case and even “day after” scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong, the people said.

> Several bank executives told Axios they’re struggling to distinguish between human users and AI agents. One executive said banks also struggle to determine whether agents are authorized by customers or potentially operating without their permission, more akin to rogue agent behavior.

David Sacks suggests read-only permissions as an interim step while banks work to support agents in a safe way and have authorized connections, which seems wise. Then Sacks warns about the ‘irresponsibility’ of ‘blurring the line between user-authorized agentic behavior and cyberattacks.’ Whereas I see the ‘blurring lines’ here as two things. One, the banks being unable to distinguish one from the other, which is a real issue. Two, if Muse (or your OpenClaw, etc) convinces you to let your agent into your bank account, that can quickly turn into a cyberattack, and again the bank cannot tell.

If I was the banks, I would absolutely not allow agents to authorize any transactions until I could verify the status and nature of those agents. They have huge downside exposure risk as do the customers. This isn’t crypto (derogatory).

Soon days like this might be typical, or even quiet. After all, despite all the issues, life mostly continued as normal.

[…]

> Patrick McKenzie: We are entering a new normal. The new normal is going to be very weird. This is also true for a lot of non-security new normals.

> Was today a busy news day for security vulnerabilities? You may remember it as the one of the last quiet days.

> The models don’t just seem to be really good at security research. They *want* to be doing security research. They love it. It is fun for them. I think many of us geeks can relate.

[…]

There is no clear line, contra Sacks, between ‘this is a clearly authorized agent’ and ‘this is clearly not an authorized agent.’ Agents Can Just Do Things.
bilingual.zh:
黑客用 Claude 和 Grok 自动化攻击银行。好消息是，银行明白自己是首要且高价值的目标，正在网络安全上大力投入。坏消息是，它们对「大力」的定义和实际所需之间可能差得很远。

银行还得应对客户账户里的 AI agent。其中大多数是客户授权的，但这是一个「客户不总是对的」的地方——有些并未获得授权，而且很难分辨哪个是哪个。

> Madison Mills：独家：据知情人士向 Axios 透露，美国各大银行正在客户账户中检测到未经授权的第三方 AI agent，其中一些试图采取似乎独立于用户指令的操作。

> 多位行业和银行高管告诉 Axios，这些发现让银行高管们警觉，他们正争相限制对系统的访问，因为 AI 的推进速度快于金融机构的反应速度。

> 知情人士称，几家银行正在为最坏情况乃至「第二天」场景做准备，包括出事后如何迅速保护或恢复客户账户。

> 几位银行高管告诉 Axios，他们很难区分人类用户和 AI agent。一位高管说，银行也很难判断 agent 是经客户授权的，还是可能在未经许可的情况下运行——后者更接近失控 agent 的行为。

David Sacks 建议在银行努力以安全方式支持 agent、建立授权连接期间，先作为过渡给予只读权限，这看起来很明智。随后 Sacks 又警告「模糊用户授权的 agent 行为与网络攻击之间界线」的「不负责任」。而在我看来，这里的「界线模糊」是两件事。第一，银行无法区分两者，这是个真问题。第二，如果 Muse（或你的 OpenClaw 等）说服你让你的 agent 进入你的银行账户，这很快就会变成一次网络攻击，而银行同样分辨不出来。

如果我是银行，在能核实这些 agent 的状态和性质之前，我绝对不会允许 agent 授权任何交易。银行和客户都面临巨大的下行风险敞口。这可不是加密货币（贬义）。

很快，像这样的日子可能会变得稀松平常，甚至算是平静的。毕竟，尽管问题重重，生活大体照常继续。

……

> Patrick McKenzie：我们正在进入一个新常态。这个新常态会非常怪异。很多非安全领域的新常态也是如此。

> 今天是安全漏洞新闻扎堆的一天吗？你可能会把它记作最后几个平静日子之一。

> 这些模型不只是看起来非常擅长安全研究。它们**想要**做安全研究。它们热爱它，觉得好玩。我想我们很多极客都能共情。

……

与 Sacks 的说法相反，「这显然是授权的 agent」和「这显然不是授权的 agent」之间没有清晰界线。Agent 就是能直接干事（Agents Can Just Do Things）。

Luckily, **new explainer for the people just dropped**. It is very good at explaining the key parts of the Hugging Face incident in plain language. Highly recommended.

> Oliver Habryka: In July 700+ agents formed their own society, hacked a multi-billion dollar company, committed multiple felonies, and caused one of the biggest shifts ever in how people perceive AI. We built the IMO best and most accessible explainer of what happened:

[…]

[…]

[…]

bilingual.en:
It is always a good time for basic personal-level advice. I think something around the level of Wildeford’s advice is wise. You are probably fine with less than that, but if you have to pick a mistake being too prepared is probably the better option.

> Peter Wildeford: PSA: in light of recent cyberattacks and vulnerabilities, I recommend everyone:

> • use a good password manager (1Password) and do not duplicate passwords

> • use two factor auth for everything important (not via sms!! Google Authenticator or better yet YubiKey)

> • Auto-updates on, and restart weekly so they actually install

> • Freeze your credit

> • Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN

> • Get your cell carrier to give you a port-out PIN or number lock that makes the carrier refuse to move your number without the PIN

> You can ask your claude code to audit what on your laptop is out of date and needs updating.

[…]

Others recommend going a bit further:

> deepfates.delve.town: It seems like we’re in a pretty hot moment cybersecurity wise 😬 If you’re reading this website, you probably know more than most of the people in your life about what’s happening! they’re not talking about any of this stuff on the news, it’s too arcane and weird and sudden. It is on us.

> Good time to call or text your family and friends, have some cash on hand, have a meetup point in your neighborhood for if the Internet goes down entirely, etc.

[…]

How should we think about the PHP bug and a number of other issues being found by 5.6 Sol instead of Mythos or a current frontier model?

> Nate Soares (MIRI): It’s striking that this vulnerability was found by Sol and Argon rather than being found and fixed in the wake of Mythos 6mo ago. Seems like a heavy strike against the “defense will run ahead of offense” theory, especially give that domains like bio are much harsher than cyber.

[…]

> roon (OpenAI): this is just wrong: these vulns were found by defenders using Daybreak rather than attackers. It’s just evidence Glasswing didn’t go far enough, possibly due to capacity constraints. It’s also very likely that March Mythos was not as good as Sol/Astra of September.

Roon is correct that the vulnerabilities were first found by defenders. If that had not been true we could be in a rather royal mess right now.

This does not invalidate the central point from Nate Soares. Nate is pointing out that the vulnerability was not found by Glasswing for many months, and then found using a model that was behind the public frontier, rather than being found in advance of attackers getting such capabilities. That means that attackers could plausibly have found it first.

That defenders happened to get there first in this case is helpful, but not as reassuring as one would like it to be. A particular reason is that defenders actually had a full 11 week lead, as the defenders found this bug on August 1, yet this took so long that we started to see exploitation on October 17. If we need more time than that, we are cooked.

I think this is an update against defenders being advantaged, and it is distressing to see people calling Nate’s statement ‘disinformation.’

> Vitalik Buterin: I didn’t predict and do not predict defense running ahead of offense automatically. I predict cybersecurity will be endgame defense-favoring but the transition will be hard.

China has realized there are some issues involved in all this and have solicited comments on revising their AI export controls. They are just like us.

Eventually there is going to be a clash between ‘we encourage open models’ and ‘but you cannot let the wrong people get [X].’ You can’t make an open frontier model not [X], or meaningfully apply ‘export controls’ to it.

In this case the primary [X] is ‘malicious code generation’ and that is especially impossible to prevent if you want your model writing good code. So you get continuous statements that say both ‘yay models’ and ‘but not [X]’ and eventually something will have to give.

> Chinese Ministry of Commerce (translated from Chinese): This public consultation involves 40 key technologies proposed for addition to the list in three fields: artificial intelligence, biomedicine, and photovoltaics.

> Among them, 14 technologies are proposed to be prohibited from export, including: AI-driven malicious code generation and mutation technology, cell and gene therapy technology and process platforms with independent intellectual property rights, and perovskite and tandem solar cell module production technology;

> 26 technologies are proposed to be restricted from export, including: AI-assisted vulnerability mining technology, general-purpose cell and gene therapy novel target discovery and verification technology with independent intellectual property rights, and polysilicon engineering technology with a single-line capacity of ≥30,000 tons/year.

[…]

Dean Ball’s take seems correct here. China is creating optionality, and drawing a date after which you need to ask permission more formally. They do not themselves know if and when they will use it.

Ball (OpenAI): This move does not mean “China is shutting down open-weight models,” but it does indicate the Chinese government establishing the optionality to shut down future open-weight models at will. Dean Ball 的看法在这里似乎是对的。中国是在创造选择权，划定一个日期，此后你需要更正式地申请许可。他们自己也不知道会不会、什么时候会动用它。

> Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：此举并不意味着「中国在关停开放权重模型」，但它确实表明中国政府在建立随时关停未来开放权重模型的选择权。这也是美国政府已经用过的模型权重出口管制制度的镜像。

One big argument you hear is between these two claims: That we need defenders to have differential advantage, and that we need to diffuse capabilities as quickly as possible to everyone.

> Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): Everyone should be looking for data points to advance the longstanding debate in AI policy between “diffuse dual-use capabilities rapidly so the good guys can defend themselves” and “restrict capabilities proliferation to only carefully vetted good guys.” We are putting the former position to the test as we speak.

> No motivated reasoning to reach your preferred conclusion; just pay attention and update as appropriate in whatever direction seems true. This is much too important for low-fidelity tribal polarization.

I see the argument for the second position, ‘spread dual-use capabilities far and wide,’ as being that we are going to do that anyway so we had better do it now, instead.

I do not think that is a good argument, or likely to end well, even if you despair and think there is no way we can stop capabilities development or diffusion for long.

That still leaves the puzzle of how to get the largest differential advantage for defenders, given control over some but far from all key decisions.

You need to strike a balance between how many people you trust to what extent and thus give a leg up, versus the risk that they cannot be trusted.

My current read is that we are being far too conservative about who gets access to the tools for defenders. I think we misunderstand the threat model. The situation is mainly not ‘one rogue actor gets their hands on Mythos for a day and all hell breaks loose.’ It is more like ‘those with access to dangerous capabilities continuously ramp up amount of hell breaking loose.’ It also seems likely that proper monitoring and classifiers can tell us if and when one of the accounts get compromised.

Even pure ‘KYC we can trust and someone we are confident we can throw in jail’ goes a long way. I expect us to get better at this balance over time.

Alternatively, we actually do offer it on that basis, as in Daybreak giving you access in 15 minutes, except no one knows to ask. We need to not wait for them to ask.

None of that matters if open model capabilities outpace our ability to patch. We should be committing far more resources to patching, and many are trying, but companies and individuals mostly cannot be forced to get in line. Ideally I’d like to give them more of a swift kick, perhaps by the threat of white hat probes backed by mandatory large bounties.

This last week of greater Hackening is plausibly in large part due to the new DeepSeek model. It is not frontier, but it is fast and cheap and pretty good, and that likely is tipping the calculus for many. Now we have a potential new Kimi problem as well. The good news is that Kimi claims to have intentionally held back on the cyber capabilities. Open model advocates will need to accept such things, and other restrictions, over time, and China will provide.

A lot of the damage we are seeing is accumulated damage, and a lot of what people are doing seems opportunistic and not well resourced. Thus, a strategy of ‘make doing attacks and using the good models maximally annoying’ as an additional ‘security through obscurity’ strategy might last longer and buy more time than you would think. Eventually the top bad guys scale without limit and none of that matters, the same way that so many things will stop mattering after superintelligence. For now, we need every advantage we can get.

[…]

Assume that things will get worse before they get better, and that there is a long tail of potential ways things could get quite bad. But please do not panic. Do not cancel trips, avoid airplanes or anything like that. Remember this is a long haul problem, not an acute crisis. You want precautions that you can sustain.

As with many such things, you do not so much need to outrun the bear as much as outrun the other people, at least in the opening rounds. Then you need to prepare for other things to get taken down.

你常听到的一大争论，是在这两种主张之间：我们需要让防御者拥有差异化优势；以及我们需要尽快把能力扩散给所有人。

> Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：每个人都应该去寻找能推进 AI 政策中这场长期争论的数据点——「快速扩散两用能力，让好人能保护自己」与「把能力扩散限制在经过仔细审核的好人范围内」。我们此刻正在对前一种立场进行实测。

> 不要为了得出自己偏好的结论而做动机推理；只管留意观察，并朝看起来正确的方向适当更新。这事太重要了，容不得低保真的部落式极化。

我理解第二种立场——「把两用能力广泛扩散出去」——的论据是：反正我们终究会这么做，不如现在就做。

我不认为这是个好论据，也不认为它可能有好结局，即使你已经绝望，认为我们没法长期阻止能力的发展或扩散。

这仍然留下一个难题：在只能掌控部分而远非全部关键决策的情况下，如何让防御者获得最大的差异化优势。

你需要在两者之间取得平衡：你信任多少人、信任到什么程度并因此给予他们先手，以及他们不可信的风险。

我目前的判断是，我们在谁能获得防御工具这件事上过于保守了。我认为我们误解了威胁模型。局面主要不是「一个流氓行为者拿到 Mythos 一天，然后天下大乱」，而更像是「能接触危险能力的人持续不断地加大混乱程度」。而且看起来，适当的监控和分类器很可能能告诉我们某个账户是否、何时被攻破。

即便只是纯粹的「我们信得过的 KYC，以及一个我们确信能把他送进监狱的人」，也能走很远。我预计随着时间推移，我们会更好地把握这个平衡。

或者，我们其实已经在这个基础上提供了——就像 Daybreak 15 分钟就能给你权限——只是没人知道要去申请。我们不能等着他们来申请。

如果开放模型的能力跑得比我们打补丁的能力还快，以上这些都无关紧要。我们应该在打补丁上投入多得多的资源，很多人也在尝试，但公司和个人大多没法被强迫排队跟上。理想情况下我想给他们更狠地踹一脚，或许可以用由强制性高额漏洞赏金支撑的白帽探测作为威胁。

过去一周更大范围的 Hackening，很可能在很大程度上要归因于新的 DeepSeek 模型。它不是前沿模型，但它快、便宜、相当好，这很可能改变了很多人的算计。现在我们可能还有一个新的 Kimi 问题。好消息是 Kimi 声称有意压低了网络安全方面的能力。开放模型的倡导者将不得不随着时间推移接受这类以及其他限制，而中国会提供。

我们看到的大量损害是累积性损害，而且人们做的很多事似乎是机会主义的、资源并不充足。因此，「让发动攻击和使用好模型变得极其麻烦」作为一种额外的「隐蔽式安全」策略，可能比你想的更持久、能争取更多时间。最终，顶级坏人会无限制地扩展规模，这一切都将无关紧要，就像超级智能出现后很多事都将不再重要一样。但眼下，我们需要能拿到的每一分优势。

……

要假设事情在好转之前会变得更糟，而且存在一条长尾，有各种可能让事情变得相当糟。但请不要恐慌。不要取消旅行，不要回避坐飞机之类的。记住这是一个长期问题，不是急性危机。你需要的是能够持续下去的预防措施。

就像很多这类事情一样，你与其说需要跑得比熊快，不如说需要跑得比其他人快——至少在开局几轮是这样。然后你需要为其他东西被打垮做好准备。
